reasoning: EINTR means every operation can be restarted identically. Refute this explanation with the smallest relevant state or execution.
State valid inputs, operation pre/postconditions, object ownership/lifetime and failure/publication boundaries for the specified mechanism.
Account for resource bounds and progress/complexity under the declared participant, storage and target assumptions. Name genuinely inapplicable costs instead of inventing them.

deliverables.D1: Pre-experiment prediction and causal argument addressing: EINTR means every operation can be restarted identically.
deliverables.D2: For read, write, waitpid, connect and close, distinguish interrupted-before-progress, partial progress and uncertain completion using the selected OS contracts. Implement retries only for the copier and wait operation after preserving their state.
deliverables.D3: Exact commands or derivation steps, original inputs, observed outputs, a minimized disagreement and an independent control for this leaf. Retain unsupported-tool/target outcomes separately.
deliverables.D4: Change the environment to an OS whose interrupted-close rule differs; revise the interface wrapper rather than importing Linux behavior.

verification.pass: Every task clause and the expected causal argument must be supported by the actual learner artifact/trace. A matching number with the stated misconception, missing ownership boundary or unsupported target claim fails this objective.
verification.limits: Authored per-leaf work is unattempted. Named laboratory anchors cover only their explicit cases. Newly executed lifecycle tests are assessor-reference evidence, not learner completion or the full project.
